summary.headline: Kiri Industries Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 48% YoY to INR 288 crore, with EBITDA turning positive at INR 7 crore on H-Acid price spike.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 288 crore (up 48% YoY), with material margin at 29.1% versus 26.4% a year earlier and EBITDA of about INR 7 crore (2.4% margin) against a loss of INR 14 crore. Consolidated Q2 revenue was INR 299 crore (up 40%), EBITDA about INR 2 crore, and loss after tax INR 39 crore before associates, which included a non-cash treasury fair-value loss of INR 57 crore. Management said H-Acid price gains were only partly reflected because of earlier fixed-price orders, with the benefit expected to flow into Q3 and Q4. Copper and fertilizer project phase one remains on track for 1H FY28, and the company took a 40% stake in Makilala Mining in the Philippines.

segments.name: Dyes and dye intermediates (standalone and JV)
segments.commentary: Q2 standalone material margin improved to 29.1%, but sequential material margin was hit by a narrower price-cost spread in dye intermediates. Intermediate capacity utilisation is below 60%, and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively.

segments.name: Copper and fertilizer project
segments.commentary: Equipment deliveries have started at site, with civil, foundation and structural works progressing. Phase one is on track for 1H FY28, and downstream facilities are due to be operational next fiscal year.

segments.name: Makilala Mining (Philippines, 40%)
segments.commentary: Expected to produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, of which about 100,000 t would come to India, covering roughly 6-7% of the company's 1.6 million t requirement from 2028-29.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to show significantly higher performance than Q1 and Q2 as H-Acid price gains flow into dye realisations with a one-to-two-quarter lag.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of at least 8-10% on consolidated dye revenue of INR 1,300-1,500 crore at peak; Q2 margin was about 3-4%.
H-Acid prices are expected to stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices; no visibility of China stabilisation before March 2027.
Demand for dyes and intermediates is expected to stay stable through 2H FY27.

Downstream copper facilities of about 2.6 lakh t are targeted for operation next fiscal year; smelter and fertiliser units are targeted for 2028-29. Post-start production guidance is 5 lakh t copper and 11 lakh t fertiliser.
Around 80% of copper concentrate and semi-finished requirements are said to be secured through LME-week supplier discussions.
capex_capacity: Makilala MCB project capex is about USD 280 million; Kiri's equity share is expected to be a little above USD 40 million, with the balance to come from strategic partner equity, domestic partner equity and debt (still under evaluation).
Intermediate capacity is operating below 60% because of raw material shortages, and management is working to raise utilisation for merchant sales.
India H-Acid capacity is about 60,000 t a year against domestic consumption of about 30,000-40,000 t a year.
Phase one of the integrated copper and fertiliser project is on track to start in 1H FY28; equipment deliveries have begun.
Acquired 40% in Makilala Mining Company Inc (Philippines) and incorporated Andamina SPA in Chile during the quarter.
demand_pricing: H-Acid prices have moved from about INR 400-500/kg to INR 1,600-1,800 over the last three to four weeks, per management, with China output below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t requirement due to continuous-nitration regulation.
Vinyl sulphone is above INR 450, but input costs (sulphur, aniline) have risen sharply, so spreads have not expanded proportionately.
Reactive dye prices are around INR 1,500-1,600, and dye prices follow intermediate prices with a two-to-three-month lag.
Over 50% of dye sales are exported; the company has a two-to-three-month running order book.
Dystar remains a major customer, and Lonsen Kiri is its single largest global supplier.
Copper cathodes: duty-free Japanese imports of about 200,000 t a year are insufficient, so other origins with duty are needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated EBITDA still weak despite the H-Acid price rise, and are Philippine legal costs a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal expenses in Q2 were under INR 3 crore and not the main reason. The lag comes from earlier fixed-price dye orders, with the price effect expected to show in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri appoint a CEO or CFO at Makilala to get operational control?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiri is a minority holder but sits on the board. A new management team was jointly appointed with the partner, including a CEO, Yulo Parese, formerly of Carmen Copper, and a new CFO, and Kiri has deputed staff through Carabao Corporation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H-Acid disruption in China last, and what is the cost structure of continuous nitration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China output is below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t need. Visibility is absent before March 2027, and prices may stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices. Continuous nitration adds capex, not operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri shift its strategy toward selling intermediates?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Dyes are the core business and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively. Spot sales of intermediates are opportunistic and only occur after dye orders are met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and equity requirement for Makilala, and what is its production profile?
qa_highlights.answer: The MCB project capex is about USD 280 million, with Kiri's equity a little above USD 40 million. Makilala would produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, with about 100,000 t coming to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will copper price moves affect the project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the LME-minus-to-LME-plus spread is constant, and purchases and sales are hedged through a dedicated desk, so the exposure is operational rather than price-driven.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H-Acid prices holding, and a China capacity restart could reverse the spread gains.
Standalone PAT is heavily affected by mark-to-market treasury losses (INR 57 crore in Q2).
Litigation: Celsius has appealed the arbitration awards linked to the Makilala stake.
Funding for the USD 280 million Makilala project is still being evaluated (equity versus debt split).
Preferential allotment at INR 475 per share is still in progress; a shareholder asked for a rights issue instead.
Dye prices are passed through with a two-to-three-month lag, so Q3 is only partially expected to reflect the H-Acid increase.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term copper and fertiliser growth path and on H-Acid pricing, but cautious and somewhat defensive on near-term consolidated margins, which it attributes to order lags. Management gave specific forward figures (8-10% margin target, Q3/Q4 recovery) but was vague on China's timing and on the funding structure for Makilala.
key_quotes: The project remains on track for phase one commencing in first half FY'2028.
So, quarter 3 and quarter 4, both will have significantly higher performance compared to quarter 1 and Quarter 2, where the absorption has taken place.

It is 100% hedge business on the purchase and sale side so that you do not either make anything on the higher fluctuation, on the higher side or you do not lose anything on the lower fluctuation, on the lower side but your spread continues to remain constant and consistent.

rows.label: Volume growth
